title: Growth & depreciation
examples: Teacher, if something depreciates by ten percent each year, how do I find its value after five years?
What is the difference between exponential growth and simple percentage decrease?
Can you show me an example of something growing by a percentage over many years?

explain.say: Today we look at how things change by a percentage over time. This is called growth or depreciation. We use a multiplier to make these calculations easier.
If something grows by a percentage, you find the multiplier by adding the percentage rate to one. For example, a ten percent growth means a multiplier of one point one.
To find the value after several years, you multiply the starting amount by this multiplier for each year. So, the formula is initial amount times the multiplier to the power of time.

items: Raise to the power of time

explain.say: Let us look at depreciation, which is when something loses value. If an item depreciates by twenty percent, the multiplier is one minus zero point two, which is zero point eight.
For a half-life problem, you are finding the amount remaining after half the original amount has decayed. This is a specific type of depreciation calculation.

faq.q: If the rate is negative, do I still add it to one?
faq.a: No, if the rate is negative, you must subtract it from one. For example, a ten percent decrease means you subtract zero point one from one.
asks: If it goes down by ten percent, what do I do?

faq.q: Does the multiplier change every year?
faq.a: If the percentage change is constant, the multiplier stays the same every year. You use the same multiplier repeatedly over the time period.
asks: Do I use the same number each year?

faq.q: What is the difference between using a multiplier and just multiplying by the percentage?
faq.a: Multiplying by the multiplier gives you the final amount directly. Just finding the percentage only tells you how much the value changed, not what it ended at.
asks: Why can't I just find the percentage change?
What does the multiplier actually represent?

faq.q: When should I use the half-life method?
faq.a: You use this method when the substance decays by exactly half of its current amount over a fixed time period. This is common in science topics.
asks: When do I use the half-life formula?

faq.q: If I want to know how many years until something reaches a certain value, what do I do?
faq.a: You would need to use logarithms to solve for the exponent, which represents the number of years. This is a more advanced calculation.
asks: Can I solve for the time period?

facts: Growth is calculated by multiplying the starting amount by a multiplier greater than one.
Depreciation is calculated by multiplying the starting amount by a multiplier less than one.
A half-life means the remaining amount is exactly one half of the starting amount.
The multiplier for a ten percent increase is one point one.

quiz.say: A population of bacteria starts at one hundred and grows by ten percent each year. What is the population after two years?
quiz.why: The multiplier for ten percent growth is one point one. You raise this to the power of two years and multiply it by the start value of one hundred.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you only multiplied by the rate once, ignoring the second year's growth.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you added the percentage increase twice instead of multiplying by the multiplier.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it treats the growth as simple addition rather than compounding growth.

quiz.say: A car valued at twenty thousand pounds depreciates by twenty percent each year. What is its value after one year?
quiz.why: A twenty percent decrease means the multiplier is one minus zero point two, which is zero point eight. Multiplying twenty thousand by zero point eight gives the correct value.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only calculated the amount of depreciation, not the final value.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only subtracted twenty percent from the original amount once.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you calculated the percentage decrease incorrectly.

quiz.say: If a substance has a half-life of twenty years, what fraction of the original amount remains after two half-lives?

options.show: one minus two times the half-life rate
options.say: one minus two times the half-life rate

quiz.why: After one half-life, it is one half. After the second half-life, you take half of that remaining amount, which is one quarter.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the fractions instead of multiplying them together.
wrong.1: This is wrong because half-life problems require division, not subtraction involving the time period.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it only accounts for the first half-life period.
